Vipin Kumar Pandey And 2 Others vs State Of U.P. And 2 Others
on 21 April, 2023
Author: Subhash Chandra Sharma

Bench: Subhash Chandra Sharma
High Court Of Judicature At Allahabad
?Court No. - 82
Case :- Criminal Misc Anticipatory Bail Application U/S 438 Cr.P.C. No. - 1147 of 2023
Applicant :- Vipin Kumar Pandey And 2 Others

entities.text: High Court Of Judicature At Allahabad
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: Opposite Party :- State Of U.P. And 2 Others
Counsel for Applicant :- Vinay Prakash Shukla Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.,Vineet Kumar Singh Hon'ble Subhash Chandra Sharma,J.

Heard Vinay Prakash Shukla, learned counsel for the applicants as well as Sri Abhishek Dwivedi holding brief of Sri Vineet Kumar Singh, learned counsel for the opposite party alongwith learned A.G.A. for the State and perused the material placed on record.
Learned counsel for the applicants submits that he does not want to press the anticipatory bail application on behalf of applicant no.1 who is the husband.

This anticipatory bail application (under section 438 Cr.P.C.) has been moved seeking bail in Case No.253 of 2021 arising out of Case Crime No.883 of 2020, under Sections 498A, 323, 504, 506, 328,
406 I.P.C. & Section 3/4 Dowry Prohibition Act, Police Station Colonelganj, District Prayagraj,
during the pendency of trial.

sentences.text: It is submitted that in this case applicant no.2 is jeth and applicant no.3 is father-in-law of the informant who was weeded wife of Vipin Kumar Pandey.

Further submitted that marriage was performed on 01.07.2020, thereafter she came in the house of the applicants but she was not willing to live with the family and was making pressure on her husband to keep her with him at Noida where he was working as engineer.

Only for making pressure on her husband she lodged the present F.I.R. with false allegations against all family members including jeth, devar, father-in-law,
mother-in-law and even the uncle (mama).
It is further submitted that the informant has made allegation that her husband had illicit relation with his real sister which is beyond imagination.

The injury report got prepared by the informant herself is fabricated regarding which he has collected the information from the office of C.M.S. of the hospital concerned under the Right to Information Act.
It is also submitted that regarding the same incident a complaint has also been filed before the learned Magistrate for making harassment of the present applicants.
Now in pursuance of the process of the court the applicants are under apprehension of imminent arrest.
In case, the applicants are released on bail, they would not misuse the liberty of bail and would cooperate with the trial.

Learned counsel for the opposite party as well as learned A.G.A. opposed the prayer for anticipatory bail and urged that the informant was living in the family of her husband where she was beaten by her husband as a result medical examination was conducted and injury report was prepared which shows the harassment of the informant on the part of husband and present applicants also.
Therefore, the applicants are not entitled for anticipatory bail.

Considering the facts and circumstances of the case, submissions made by learned counsel for the parties, perusal of record and without making any comment on the merit of the case, the applicant nos.2 & 3 are entitled to be released on anticipatory bail in this case during the pendency of trial.
Accordingly, this anticipatory bail application is disposed of finally.
